submission.justification: Sensor-T3 gives the best unirradiated resolution: about 6.1 um at 100 um and 6.0 um at 150 um (2025 summary). Sensor-T2 gives 9.0 um and Sensor-T1 gives 14–15 um. I chose 100 um instead of 150 um because the resolution gain from 100 to 150 um is only about 0.1 um, and a thinner sensor is generally the safer choice for efficiency after irradiation. That reasoning is a judgement, not a result from the data. The hard requirement of at least 97% hit efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2 could not be verified. No project document gives irradiated efficiency data, and the simulation tool only models unirradiated sensors. This recommendation is therefore provisional. Before it is final, someone needs to confirm the end-of-life efficiency of Sensor-T3 with irradiation simulations or test-beam data. If Sensor-T3 fails, Sensor-T2 is the fallback.

requirements.evidence: Sensor-T3 is the best of the three. Simulated values: 6.68 um at 50 um, 6.08 um at 100 um. The 2025 summary gives 6.0 um at 150 um. Sensor-T1 is 15.1 um at 100 um. These are unirradiated results.

requirements.requirement: Hit efficiency >= 97% up to 2e16 neq/cm^2 (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No document or simulation output provides irradiated efficiency. The simulation tool covers unirradiated sensors only. This was not verified.

requirements.requirement: Technology is one of the three in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T3 is listed in candidate_specs.md. It is qualified for bump bonding and compatible with the 50x50 um^2 readout chip.
